title: Robust streaming JSON: escaping, chunking, deterministic retries for structured outputs
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Summary:
Models streaming structured JSON into the API sometimes produce partial or malformed chunks (broken escapes, truncated UTF-8, stray commas, incomplete arrays/objects). This ticket defines the server-side reassembly and retry semantics plus a compatibility layer for older SDKs so consumers can reliably receive valid JSON objects or deterministic fallbacks.

Problems observed:
- Chunk boundaries cut through multi-byte UTF-8 characters or escape sequences (\uXXXX, \n, \" ), leaving invalid bytes on the client.
- Models may emit trailing commas or unclosed arrays when generation is interrupted.
- Client retries cause duplicate partial messages; naive concat yields invalid JSON or duplicated keys.
- SDKs that expect line-delimited JSON (NDJSON) break when we return streaming JSON fragments.

Goals / non-goals:
- Deliver server-side incremental JSON reassembly using a streaming-safe parser that tolerates mid-token cuts and resumes with model-generated continuation tokens where possible.
- Define deterministic retry semantics (resume token + chunk sequence id) so retries are idempotent and do not produce duplication.
- Provide a compatibility layer: NDJSON fallback and a header-based opt-in for older SDKs.
- Non-goal: Changing model output formats at generation time (we must avoid requiring model code changes).

Success criteria / Acceptance tests:
- Integration tests that simulate these failure modes (UTF-8 truncation, broken escapes, truncated arrays) pass and produce valid JSON or expected fallback objects.
- Server emits a resume token per-stream and supports replay/resume within 30s of interruption with no duplication.
- SDKs (JS/python) can opt into NDJSON fallback via `Accept: application/x-ndjson` and continue to work.
- Load test: reassembly path adds <5% p99 latency overhead under typical traffic.

Proposed API/operational changes (implementation sketch):
1. Streaming metadata: include a small JSON metadata frame at stream start (not chunked) with fields: `stream_id`, `format_hint` (json_stream|ndjson), and `schema_hash` (optional).
2. Chunk envelopes: every chunk is delivered with a short header carrying `chunk_index` and `chunk_checksum` (crc32 hex) and optional `resume_token` (opaque base64).
3. Server-side reassembly: incremental parser that accepts partial bytes and attempts to repair common cases (complete escaped sequences, finishing truncated UTF-8). If repair fails after heuristics, mark stream as `truncated` and surface a validated partial JSON object (see compatibility rules).
4. Retry semantics: client supplies last-seen `resume_token` and `chunk_index` when reconnecting. Server replays from the next chunk_index. Retries during model re-generation should be idempotent: server drops already-acknowledged chunks.
5. Compatibility: when server cannot produce fully valid JSON, provide NDJSON lines where each top-level object emitted so far becomes a separate line; include `X-Stream-Warning: partial-content` header.

Notes on trade-offs:
- Stronger correctness (full JSON reconstruction) increases CPU cost and complexity of parser; we prefer a streaming incremental parser with repair heuristics but will fall back to NDJSON to avoid blocking the client.
- Adding resume tokens requires minimal changes to the transport but adds state; we'll keep tokens short (8-16 bytes opaque) and TTL-limited.

Open questions:
- TTL for resume tokens (30s vs 5 minutes)? Default 30s but configurable per-customer.
- Should we add per-chunk signatures (HMAC) for integrity? MVP: checksum only; security team to review for high-sensitivity customers.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Streaming+JSON+Reassembly+Spec
- Prototype parser: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proto/pull/87 (initial fuzzer harness included)
- SDK changes: js-sdk PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/402 (adds resume token handling)
- Load test dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming-json/reassembly-loadtests

Acceptance test plan (high level):
- Unit: incremental parser unit tests for truncated escape sequences, multi-byte UTF-8 truncation, split surrogate pairs.
- Fuzz: feed random splits to model-like generator (see repo above).
- Integration: end-to-end with streaming client reconnection flows and NDJSON fallback.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): implement server reassembly and opt-in resume token, enable for 5% of traffic under `runtime-1.20-canary` and collect errors/backpressure metrics.
- Phase 2: enable NDJSON fallback for customers with older SDKs (by header detection).
- Phase 3: GA with release `api-2026.03` once latency/regression gates are met.
updates: 2026-03-02 - Diego Ramos: Spike completed. Implemented an incremental parser prototype that handles UTF-8 truncation and completes simple escape sequences. Fuzzer found two cases with escaped unicode surrogates. See prototype PR #87.

2026-03-03 - Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed prototype; asked for deterministic retry semantics and clearer client contract for resume token TTL. Added parent issue link to broader streaming compatibility epic (ENG-9100).
2026-03-04 - Ava Chen (Design): UX note — expose 'partial' state in Console with clear warning and link to replay options. Suggested `X-Stream-Warning` header for programmatic detection.

2026-03-05 - Diego Ramos: Implemented chunk envelope with chunk_index and crc32 checksum. Integration tests for checksum mismatch added. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/streaming-proto/pull/92
2026-03-07 - Security review request filed: https://security.redwood.ai/reviews/ENG-9421. Security recommended HMAC for high-sensitivity customers; deferring for MVP (added to dependency ENG-9402).
2026-03-08 - CI results: Fuzzer regression fixed (escaped surrogate bug). Unit test coverage: 72%. Added new tests for NDJSON fallback behavior.
2026-03-09 - Diego Ramos: Performance microbenchmark: reassembly adds ~2% median and ~6% p99 under canary traffic. Within target (<5% p99 overhead) if we optimize buffer allocation. Will iterate.
